name: Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of a rapidly enlarging vascular tumor (usually kaposiform hemangioendothelioma or tufted angioma)
Severe thrombocytopenia due to platelet trapping within the tumor
Laboratory evidence of consumptive coagulopathy including hypofibrinogenemia and elevated D-dimers
Exclusion of other causes of thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a vascular tumor with associated thrombocytopenia and consumptive coagulopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging and laboratory findings; biopsy is often avoided due to bleeding risk.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically kaposiform hemangioendothelioma or tufted angioma

common.symptomName: Petechiae and ecchymoses over tumor and surrounding skin
Pain or tenderness at tumor site
Swelling and erythema over affected area

occasional.symptomName: Bleeding from tumor or mucosal sites
Limb or organ dysfunction due to tumor mass effect
Hypotension secondary to bleeding or coagulopathy

rare.symptomName: Organ failure secondary to tumor infiltration or bleeding

imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing vascular tumor with infiltrative margins
CT scan to assess tumor extent and involvement
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology consistent with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma or tufted angioma (biopsy often avoided)

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic coagulopathy without localized vascular tumor
Underlying cause usually infection, trauma, or malignancy
Laboratory findings specific to factor deficiency

redFlags: Rapid tumor enlargement with worsening thrombocytopenia
Signs of disseminated intravascular coagulation or organ failure
references: Drolet BA, Trenor CC 3rd, Brandão LR, et al. Consensus-Derived Practice Standards Plan for Complex Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
Croteau SE, Liang MG, Kozakewich HP, et al. Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: a retrospective study of treatment with vincristine. J Pediatr Hematol Oncol. 2013;35(7):e243-e249.
Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular anomalies classification: recommendations from the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
